description: Tool built for developers — code, APIs, CLIs, and technical workflows. Industry brain defines the development domain. This core defines how developer-first products are experienced.

three_js.description: Monospace character particles falling slowly like a sparse matrix. Characters are code symbols — brackets, semicolons, operators. Dark and technical.
three_js.avoid: no status pills, no hero-stat-line, no ticker strips

relationships: User belongs to a Team and owns or contributes to Projects
Repository contains Files and has Builds
Build belongs to Repository, has a Status and Logs
Deployment belongs to Build, targets an Environment
APIKey belongs to User or Project — grants API access
Log belongs to Build or Deployment
Environment belongs to Project — production, staging, development
Integration connects Project to an external service
Usage tracks API calls, compute, or storage per Project
Webhook belongs to Project, fires on events
Documentation is associated with Project or API

layout.notes: Monospace font for all code, logs, and terminal output — no exceptions. Copy button on every code block, API key, and command. Build status always visible — never buried.

avoid: Never use photography, illustration, or decorative elements anywhere
Never use a rounded bubble UI — developer tools use sharp or minimal radius
Never paginate logs — always infinite scroll with search and filter
Never auto-refresh without showing a refresh indicator and timestamp
Never hide the raw request/response — always offer a way to see raw data
Never use a modal for log viewing — always navigate to a dedicated log screen
Never truncate error messages — full error always accessible
Never use colour alone to convey status — always pair with icon and label
enforce: Build status: spinner = building, green check = success, red X = failed — always these exact patterns
Log lines in monospace font — always
Error lines in logs always red background highlight
New log lines auto-scroll to bottom — with manual scroll-lock toggle
API key always partially masked — first 4 and last 4 chars visible, rest masked
Copy to clipboard on every code snippet and API key — keyboard shortcut supported
Uptime shown as percentage with 2 decimal places — 99.98% not 'high'
Deploy time shown precisely — '2m 34s' not 'about 3 minutes'

empty_states.ui: Code terminal illustration (minimal SVG). Message: 'No projects yet'. CTA: 'Create your first project'. Show CLI command as alternative: 'or run [command] to get started'.

empty_states.trigger: No logs for this project yet
empty_states.ui: Terminal cursor blinking. Message: 'No logs yet. Logs will appear here once your project is deployed.'
Key icon. Message: 'No API keys yet'. CTA: 'Generate API key'. Warning: 'Keep your keys secure. Never share them publicly.'.

loading_states.ui: Metrics skeleton — grey rectangles same size as real values. Build list skeleton rows — status icon placeholder, project name, timestamp.
Log lines appear as they stream — never batch. First 50 lines from cache immediately. New lines append at bottom with auto-scroll.
Build steps list skeleton. Active step shows spinner. Completed steps show green check immediately — never wait for all steps.

error_flows.ui: Build status: red X. Error summary at top of build log. Failing step highlighted. Full error output below. CTA: 'View logs'. Never just 'Build failed' with no detail.
Deployment status: red. Last successful deployment still live — shown clearly. Error detail expandable. Rollback CTA prominent.
API calls return 401. Dashboard shows alert: 'Your API key has been revoked'. Instructions to generate new key. Old key not shown.
429 response shown in request log with reset time. Dashboard shows rate limit gauge. Warning before hitting limit at 80%.

edge_cases.ui: Virtualised list — only render visible lines. Search within logs. Jump to error shortcut. Download full log option.
Each environment shown as separate row with own status. Never collapse into single status when environments differ.

edge_cases.case: API key used from unexpected location
edge_cases.ui: Security alert in dashboard: 'Unusual API key usage detected from [country]'. Option to revoke immediately. Never silent.
Two rows shown — old version winding down, new version spinning up. Traffic split shown as progress bar. Both statuses visible simultaneously.
